featured.title: America Turns 250. A Million Indians Are Still Waiting for Green Cards
featured.excerpt: The country celebrates its semiquincentennial on the backs of immigrants who built $5 trillion in startup wealth — and still cannot become permanent residents.
featured.image_caption: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor — a symbol of the immigrant dream that over a million Indians are still waiting to realise
featured.nri_angle: Indian Americans are among the most successful immigrant communities in US history, yet face the longest green card backlogs — a contradiction that America's 250th birthday makes impossible to ignore.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America's 250th Birthday Was the Hottest on Record. Literally.
news.excerpt: A historic heat dome cancelled parades from Philadelphia to Boston, strained power grids to the breaking point, and forced Trump's Great American State Fair to temporarily shut its gates.
news.image_caption: Crowds gather on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. for Fourth of July celebrations near the Washington Monument
news.nri_angle: Millions of Indian Americans across the East Coast and Mid-Atlantic faced cancelled celebrations and power outages during one of the community's most visible American holiday weekends.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Own Attorney General Called E20 Fuel an 'Experiment.' The Government Spent the Next 48 Hours in Damage Control.
news.excerpt: A viral courtroom video has turned simmering consumer anger over mandatory ethanol-blended petrol into the Modi government's biggest domestic headache this summer.
news.image_caption: A BPCL petrol pump in India, where E20 ethanol-blended fuel is now the only option at nearly all stations
news.nri_angle: NRIs driving in India face the same E20 fuel with no alternative, and the auto sector uncertainty affects diaspora investments in one of India's flagship industries.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and Japan Just Signed Their First Defence Co-Development Deal. It Is the Start of Something Much Bigger.
news.excerpt: Modi and Takaichi summit in New Delhi delivered pacts on AI, stealth naval tech, critical minerals, and a $61 billion investment roadmap — reshaping what the two economies mean to each other.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan during the 16th India-Japan Annual Summit
news.nri_angle: With 1,400 Japanese firms already in India, a 10 trillion yen investment target, and new openings in AI and defence manufacturing, the summit creates direct job and investment pathways for NRI professionals and investors eyeing the India-Japan corridor.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Eight Men Arrested for Stealing Donations From the Ram Mandir. A Court Is Being Asked to Call In the CBI.
news.excerpt: CCTV footage, property raids, and a PIL seeking a CAG audit — the embezzlement scandal at Ayodhya's most sacred site is deepening by the day.
news.image_caption: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Mandir in Ayodhya, consecrated by Prime Minister Modi in January 2024
news.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs donated to the Ram Mandir construction fund, making this a deeply personal scandal for the diaspora — a PIL in the Allahabad High Court now seeks an independent CAG audit of the Trust's finances.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Turns 250 Tomorrow. No Immigrant Community Has Risen Faster Than Indian Americans.
news.excerpt: As the U.S. marks its semiquincentennial, 5.2 million Indian Americans — now the country's largest Asian ethnic group — are reshaping everything from the C-suite to Capitol Hill. Their story is also getting more complicated.
news.image_caption: July Fourth celebrations at a U.S. Embassy, marking Independence Day
news.nri_angle: Indian Americans are now the largest Asian ethnic group in the US and pay 5-6% of all income taxes despite being 1.5% of the population — the 250th anniversary is as much their celebration as anyone's.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Operation Amistad Wins Hearts in Earthquake-Shattered Venezuela
news.excerpt: Two IAF C-17 Globemasters, 41 medical personnel, and indigenous BHISHM cubes — India's disaster-relief machine reaches Latin America as the death toll crosses 2,600.
news.image_caption: An Indian Air Force aircraft being loaded with humanitarian relief supplies for deployment. India's C-17 Globemasters have become the backbone of its disaster-response operations worldwide.
news.image_credit: Indian Air Force / Government of India (GODL-India), via Wikimedia Commons
news.nri_angle: India's growing first-responder reputation across continents reinforces national pride for the diaspora and underscores New Delhi's expanding strategic engagement with Latin America.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Logged Its Driest June in Fifteen Years. The Next Two Weeks Will Decide What Millions of Farmers Eat.
news.excerpt: Kharif sowing is running 23% behind last year, El Niño is strengthening, and food prices are already climbing. The monsoon's July performance will shape inflation and rural incomes for months to come.
news.image_caption: Parched farmland during a delayed monsoon in India (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: A weak monsoon means higher food bills for families receiving NRI remittances, and potential rice export curbs that would affect diaspora communities in the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Was Personally Invited to Khamenei's Funeral. India Sent a Deputy Minister Instead.
news.excerpt: As Iran stages a week of mass processions for its slain Supreme Leader, India's carefully calibrated delegation reveals the diplomatic tightrope New Delhi walks between Tehran and Washington.
news.image_caption: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an official portrait released during Nowruz celebrations
news.nri_angle: The India-Iran relationship affects Strait of Hormuz negotiations, oil prices, and shipping routes that directly impact NRIs in the Gulf and Indian businesses across the Middle East.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Scrapped Taxes on Its Bonds. $3.4 Billion Poured In Within Weeks.
news.excerpt: New Delhi's most aggressive capital-market reform in years has unlocked record foreign inflows, and Bloomberg's biggest bond index could be next.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India building in Kolkata, home to the central bank that broadened bond access for foreign investors
news.nri_angle: NRI investors and the broader diaspora benefit directly from a more accessible, tax-free Indian bond market — and Bloomberg index inclusion would further deepen the pool of rupee-denominated assets available for offshore portfolios.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live in Twelve Days. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora.
news.excerpt: The India-UK CETA eliminates tariffs on 99 percent of Indian exports, opens 137 service sectors, and ends double social security payments for 75,000 professionals. It enters force on July 15.
news.image_caption: UK Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds and India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal sign the India-UK trade agreement

sources.label: Press Information Bureau, Government of India

news.nri_angle: The Double Contribution Convention ending dual social security payments directly saves Indian professionals in the UK thousands of pounds annually, while 1,800 visas for chefs, yoga instructors, and musicians create new mobility pathways.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Adani and Abu Dhabi Are Building a $11.5 Billion Aluminium Complex in Odisha. It Would Be India's Biggest Foreign Metals Investment Ever.
news.excerpt: The 50:50 joint venture with the UAE's IHC will produce 2 million metric tons of aluminium a year, create 53,500 jobs, and raise India's smelting capacity by half. The announcement comes as a US judge keeps Adani's criminal case alive.
news.image_caption: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group
news.nri_angle: The massive Gulf-India industrial tie-up signals deepening economic integration between India and the UAE, while the US court proceedings over Adani's alleged bribery scheme remain a governance concern for NRI investors holding Adani Group securities.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Is Heading to Three Countries Next Week. In One of Them, Indians Are Being Told They're Not Welcome.
news.excerpt: The PM's six-day tour covers Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand — where a historic first visit in 40 years collides with anti-Indian immigration crackdowns and planned protests.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese at a bilateral meeting
news.nri_angle: One million Indian-born Australians, 250,000 Indians in New Zealand, and a historic PM visit colliding with targeted anti-Indian immigration rules make this tour deeply personal for the diaspora.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Foreign Money Is Leaving India's Stock Market at a Record Pace. For the First Time in Two Decades, Indian Investors Don't Need It.
news.excerpt: The RBI's latest Financial Stability Report reveals FPI ownership at a 20-year low of 16%, with domestic investors commanding 20% — and new rules now let NRIs own even more.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai — the epicentre of India's equity markets where domestic investors now hold more sway than foreign funds for the first time in two decades.
news.nri_angle: RBI raised equity investment limits for NRIs and OCIs as part of measures to attract overseas capital, giving the diaspora broader access to Indian markets at corrected valuations
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Services Engine Just Hit Its Slowest Speed in Seventeen Months. The Hiring Freeze Is the Bigger Story.
news.excerpt: The HSBC India Services PMI fell to 57.4 in June as domestic demand weakened sharply and only 1% of firms added staff — a dramatic retreat from the hiring boom of April and May.
news.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, India's financial capital
news.nri_angle: A weakening services sector in India directly threatens the IT outsourcing industry that employs millions of NRIs and underpins H-1B visa sponsorship pipelines to the US, UK and Canada.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: AI Hiring in India Just Surged 16%. The Rest of the IT Industry Is Shrinking.
news.excerpt: A Naukri report shows AI roles grew 16% year-on-year in June while overall IT jobs fell 3% — the clearest sign yet that India's $315 billion tech sector is splitting into two economies.
news.image_caption: Aerial view of the glass pyramid at the Infosys campus in Bangalore, India's IT capital
news.nri_angle: Indian IT professionals on H-1B visas work disproportionately in the traditional services roles being automated — the AI-versus-IT split directly shapes their career security and immigration prospects.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Let Four Chinese Power Equipment Firms Bid for Government Contracts. Five Years of Frozen Relations Are Thawing Fast.
news.excerpt: A Finance Ministry order gives TBEA Energy, Nanjing Electric India and two other Chinese-linked manufacturers a two-year exemption to compete for critical power tenders — the latest in a calibrated reset with Beijing.
news.image_caption: An electrical power substation in Sambalpur, Odisha, India
news.nri_angle: NRIs in U.S. energy and infrastructure sectors should watch the India-China power equipment thaw closely — it reshapes both the competitive landscape and collaboration opportunities in India's energy transition.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: CRED's Kunal Shah Is Now Running WhatsApp. Meta Paid $900 Million to Make It Happen.
news.excerpt: The Indian founder who turned credit card bills into a fintech empire now leads the world's biggest messaging app. It's the most consequential Indian tech appointment since Satya Nadella.
news.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and newly appointed global head of WhatsApp (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: An Indian founder — not an Indian-American corporate executive — now leads the platform that is the primary communication channel between the diaspora and home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Has Now Served Notices to Every Major Messaging App Over Usernames. The Crackdown Is Widening.
news.excerpt: After freezing WhatsApp's username rollout, the government is now demanding answers from Telegram and Signal. Indian platform Arattai has already surrendered the feature entirely.
news.image_caption: A user texting on WhatsApp, India's dominant messaging platform with over 500 million users
news.nri_angle: Diaspora Indians who rely on WhatsApp, Telegram, and Signal to communicate with family could see privacy features limited if India forces platforms to tie usernames to verified phone numbers.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indiaspora Just Catalogued 250 Milestones of Indian American Life. The Timing Is Not a Coincidence.
nri-world.excerpt: Released two days before America's 250th birthday, the compilation spans motel lobbies, yoga studios, Fortune 500 boardrooms — and asks who still gets left out of the story.
nri-world.image_caption: M.R. Rangaswami, founder and chairman of Indiaspora, at a diaspora event
nri-world.nri_angle: A definitive compilation of how Indian Americans have shaped the United States across 15 domains — from hospitality and tech to philanthropy and civil rights — released as America marks its semiquincentennial.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Modi Is Taking His Diaspora Playbook to Three Countries in Six Days. In One of Them, It Will Be Tested.
nri-world.excerpt: A million Indians in Australia, a 40-year gap in New Zealand, and the 'butter chicken tsunami' that won't go away — inside the Indo-Pacific tour that starts Monday.
nri-world.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, whose six-day Indo-Pacific tour begins July 6
nri-world.nri_angle: Modi's three-nation tour includes large-scale diaspora addresses in every stop, but the NZ leg puts a spotlight on rising anti-Indian sentiment and hate crimes that have left the community feeling targeted.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: They Started Fighting for India in Westminster During the Emergency. Fifty Years Later, They Want Blue Plaques.
nri-world.excerpt: FISI UK, the oldest Indian advocacy organisation in Britain, celebrated its golden jubilee with a new initiative to map every Indian trailblazer who lived on British soil.
nri-world.image_caption: The Bhavan Indian Arts Centre in West Kensington, London — venue for the FISI UK Golden Jubilee
nri-world.nri_angle: FISI UK was founded by British Indians in 1976 to give the diaspora a political voice in Westminster. Its 50-year journey mirrors the trajectory of the British Indian community itself — from political invisibility to mainstream influence. The SMRITI initiative now aims to preserve that history for future generations.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two Duke Cardiologists Now Lead the American Heart Association. Both Are Children of Indian Immigrants.
nri-world.excerpt: Dr. Manesh Patel becomes the first South Asian to serve as AHA volunteer president. His president-elect, Dr. Svati Shah, runs one of the country's leading precision cardiovascular genetics programmes. Both start July 1.
nri-world.image_caption: Duke Chapel on the Duke University campus in Durham, North Carolina — home institution of Dr. Manesh Patel and Dr. Svati Shah, now leading the American Heart Association
nri-world.nri_angle: Two Indian-American doctors simultaneously leading the AHA marks a generational milestone for a community that is overrepresented in medicine but underrepresented in legacy medical leadership. South Asians also face disproportionately high cardiovascular risk, making this appointment personally significant for the diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New Zealand Signed a Trade Deal With India. Then It Quietly Started Writing Immigration Rules That Apply to Indians — and Only Indians.
nri-world.excerpt: Even NZ's own Foreign Minister calls the proposed restrictions discriminatory. Days before Modi's first-ever visit, the country's coalition government is tearing itself apart over who gets to come in.
nri-world.image_caption: New Zealand's Parliament House in Wellington, where the ruling coalition is divided over immigration rules that single out Indian nationals under the newly signed free trade agreement.
nri-world.nri_angle: New Zealand's proposed immigration restrictions specifically target Indian nationals, affecting NRI workers, students, and the 250,000-strong Indian diaspora community — with racist rhetoric and anti-Indian protests compounding the policy threat
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The USISPF Summit Honoured Three Business Titans. Sunil Mittal Used His Speech to Talk About Five Million Indians Instead.
nri-world.excerpt: At the IX USISPF Leadership Summit in Washington, Bharti's chairman and India's ambassador to the US laid out a vision in which the diaspora is not a footnote to the India-US partnership but the load-bearing wall.
nri-world.image_caption: Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman of Bharti Enterprises
nri-world.nri_angle: Mittal explicitly framed the 5-million-strong Indian American community as the strategic bridge between India and the US — in trade, defence, and high technology. Ambassador Kwatra's $30 trillion roadmap positions the diaspora as investors, knowledge partners, and connectors in India's climb to developed-nation status by 2047.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Sitharaman Took India's Chequebook to France. She Is Ending the Trip by Meeting the Diaspora.
nri-world.excerpt: India's finance minister co-chaired an economic dialogue in Aix-en-Provence, courted BNP Paribas and a cargo airship startup, and will wrap up her four-day visit with a community event for Indians in France — the quiet end of a loud trip.
nri-world.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman during a European engagement in 2025
nri-world.nri_angle: Sitharaman's France visit concludes with a diaspora community interaction, connecting India's economic diplomacy directly to the 30,000-strong Indian community in France. India-France trade has doubled in a decade to €13.59 billion, and the India-EU FTA signed in January 2026 opens new pathways for NRIs across Europe.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Immigrants Have Built 96 Billion-Dollar Startups in America. No Other Country Comes Close.
nri-world.excerpt: A new NFAP study finds India is the largest source of immigrant unicorn founders in the US, with 96 companies collectively worth more than Germany's stock market.
nri-world.image_caption: Jyoti Bansal, Indian-born founder of AppDynamics and Harness, at TechCrunch Disrupt 2024 — one of 96 Indian immigrant-founded US unicorn startups identified in the NFAP study (Photo: TechCrunch/Katelyn Tucker, CC BY 2.0)
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-born entrepreneurs account for 96 of America's 775 unicorns — the most of any country. Most arrived as IIT graduates on student visas, building the exact pipeline now threatened by tightening H-1B and student visa policies.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Carnegie Names Four Indian Americans to Its 'Great Immigrants' List — on the Eve of America's 250th Birthday
nri-world.excerpt: Nikesh Arora, Mahzarin Banaji, Sanjiv Chopra, and Reshma Kewalramani join a class of 25 naturalized citizens honoured by the Carnegie Corporation for the Fourth of July.
nri-world.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, one of four Indian Americans named to Carnegie's 2026 Great Immigrants list
nri-world.nri_angle: Four Indian-born leaders — spanning cybersecurity, social psychology, medicine, and biotech — are honoured as 'Great Americans' at a moment when immigration restrictions are tightening. The recognition underscores the diaspora's institutional reach across American life.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: New US Bill Would End OPT, Kill H-1B Green Card Pathway in Sweeping Overhaul
nri-world.excerpt: Rep. Chip Roy’s American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act targets every stage of the Indian professional immigration pipeline, from student work permits to permanent residency
nri-world.image_caption: The US Capitol, where Rep. Chip Roy introduced the American White-Collar Worker Jobs Act of 2026 targeting the H-1B visa program.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indians hold 72% of H-1B visas and rely on OPT and the H-1B-to-green-card pipeline that this bill would dismantle — a direct threat to the immigration pathway used by hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two Thousand Indian-Origin Doctors Just Took Over Tampa's Waterfront. The Timing Was Not an Accident.
nri-world.excerpt: AAPI's 44th annual convention opens on America's 250th birthday weekend, blending scientific sessions with a red-carpet civic reception from the City of Tampa.
nri-world.image_caption: Healthcare professionals in a hospital setting — Indian-origin physicians form one of the largest ethnic groups in American medicine
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin physicians form one of the largest ethnic groups in American medicine. AAPI's convention, timed to America's 250th, is both a professional assembly and a statement of belonging.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Nine Hundred Young Jains Just Sold Out a Convention in New Jersey. Their Theme: 'The Art of the In-Between.'
nri-world.excerpt: The 17th biennial Young Jains of America convention opens this week with 915 attendees across three age cohorts — every spot taken, every waitlist full.
nri-world.image_caption: Jain community celebrations at a temple in New York City
nri-world.nri_angle: Young Jain Americans navigate between an ancient faith built on non-violence and non-attachment and a consumer culture that runs on the opposite. YJA's sold-out convention is the infrastructure they built for that in-between.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Services Engine Just Hit Its Slowest Speed in 17 Months — and Hiring Has Nearly Stalled
markets-finance.excerpt: The HSBC India Services PMI fell sharply to 57.4 in June as domestic demand weakened to its lowest in over two years, even as export orders offered a partial cushion
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors watching the Wall Street GDP upgrades and FPI flow reversal should weigh them against the sharpest services sector deceleration in 17 months — if domestic demand and hiring stay weak, the earnings recovery that fund managers are banking on may not materialise.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: HCLTech Just Landed a $1.14 Billion AI Deal With a European Giant — Its Biggest in Three Years
markets-finance.excerpt: The mega-contract to build an AI-driven digital workplace for a Fortune Global 50 firm is entirely new business, ends a three-year drought in large deals, and lifts the Nifty IT index on a day when global tech is still reeling.
markets-finance.nri_angle: Directly relevant to the tens of thousands of Indian-origin IT professionals and NRI investors with exposure to Indian tech stocks — the deal signals that AI-led transformation is creating new revenue streams, not just destroying old ones.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreign Investors Just Poured a Record $3.4 Billion Into Indian Government Bonds — and a Bloomberg Index Entry Could Unlock Billions More
markets-finance.excerpt: India's decision to scrap taxes on foreign bond investments, combined with falling oil prices and RBI reforms, has triggered the biggest monthly debt inflow on record and put Bloomberg Global Aggregate Index inclusion within reach
markets-finance.image_caption: India's bond market is drawing record foreign investment after sweeping tax reforms
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors can now hold Indian sovereign bonds tax-free after India scrapped withholding and capital gains taxes, making the 6.7% yield one of the most attractive risk-adjusted returns in emerging markets.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: A Weak US Jobs Report Just Took a Fed Rate Hike Off the Table — and India's Markets Are Surging on the News
markets-finance.excerpt: Nonfarm payrolls came in at just 57,000 against expectations of 115,000, sending the dollar to its biggest one-day drop in two months and pushing Indian equities back above the $5 trillion mark for the first time since the Iran crisis began.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai — India's equity market has reclaimed the $5 trillion valuation mark
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with US-denominated earnings and India-allocated portfolios benefit directly from a weaker dollar and easing Fed rate fears — the macro backdrop for Indian equities is the most favourable it has been in months.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's IT Giants Face Their Most Scrutinised Earnings Season in Years — and AI Is the Elephant in Every Boardroom
markets-finance.excerpt: With the Nifty IT index down 33% from its February peak, TCS and Infosys are about to report June-quarter results that could determine whether the sector's correction is a buying opportunity or the start of a structural decline.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bangalore — India's IT bellwether reports Q1 FY27 results on July 23
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors hold significant IT sector exposure and many work in the very industry under scrutiny — this earnings season is both a portfolio and career signal.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Wall Street Just Raised India's Growth Forecast to 7% — the Sharpest Upward Revision in Over a Year
markets-finance.excerpt: Bank of America, Crisil, and Goldman Sachs have all upgraded India's outlook in the span of a week, citing collapsing oil prices, the Iran peace deal, and a capex surge — while the rupee posts its first quarterly gain since early 2025
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai — the central bank's dollar-inflow measures have helped the rupee post its first quarterly gain in over a year
markets-finance.nri_angle: Rupee stability means NRI equity and debt returns are no longer being eroded by currency depreciation; the wave of growth upgrades improves the case for India-linked portfolio allocations.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is 'Very, Very Close' to a Historic US Trade Deal — but a $500 Billion Target and New Tariffs Stand in the Way
markets-finance.excerpt: As the India-UK CETA prepares to launch on July 15, Washington says a bilateral trade agreement with New Delhi is nearly done — while a proposed 12.5% forced-labour tariff threatens to complicate the final stretch
markets-finance.image_caption: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and UK Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds sign the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement
markets-finance.nri_angle: A US deal could lower tariff costs on Indian exports and ease barriers for IT professionals, while the UK CETA eliminates double social security payments for NRIs in Britain
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's SIP Investors Refuse to Blink — ₹30,000 Crore a Month Keeps Flowing Even as Equity Fund Inflows Drop 40%
markets-finance.excerpt: Systematic investment plans held above ₹30,000 crore for three straight months through May 2026, absorbing a sharp lump-sum pullback and underlining a structural shift in how Indian retail money behaves.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Phiroze Jeejeebhoy Towers, home of the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors who use SIP channels to invest in Indian mutual funds should note that the domestic retail floor is now structurally strong enough to cushion FII selling — a dynamic that reduces the kind of sharp drawdowns that used to punish long-distance investors.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Emerging as Asia's Safe Haven as the Global AI Selloff Crushes South Korea and Taiwan
markets-finance.excerpt: With KOSPI plunging below 8,000 and foreigners dumping $137 billion of Asian equities in H1 2026, India's oil-fuelled rally and domestic-demand story are pulling global money in a new direction
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building in Mumbai, home of the Sensex
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with Asian market exposure face a historic rotation away from AI-heavy chip plays in Korea and Taiwan toward India, where oil collapse, rupee recovery, and domestic-demand sectors offer a compelling alternative.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is About to Witness Its Biggest-Ever IPO Wave — From Jio's $3.8 Billion Listing to Carlsberg's Beer Play
markets-finance.excerpt: Carlsberg has confidentially filed for a $700 million India IPO, joining a pipeline that includes Jio Platforms, NSE, PhonePe, and Pernod Ricard — collectively the largest collection of marquee listings India has ever seen in a single year
markets-finance.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, set to host what could be the country's biggest IPO wave
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors who can access Indian IPOs through demat accounts or GIFT City–routed platforms face a once-in-a-generation lineup — but the sheer volume of issuance will test whether the market can absorb it all.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indian Households Just Sold 50 Tonnes of Gold in a Single Quarter — the Sharpest Spike in Years
markets-finance.excerpt: Nearly 50 tonnes of old gold flooded back into the market in April–June 2026, a 43% jump from a year ago. For a nation that treats gold as heirloom, the shift from hoarding to liquidating signals something deeper than just falling prices.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold jewellery: Antique Indian Nose Ring Jewellery
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI families holding gold in India face rebalancing decisions as prices drop 22% from peak; the shift from physical hoarding to digital gold instruments reshapes how diaspora investors should think about gold in their Indian portfolio.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: KPIT Technologies Just Lost 17% in a Single Day — and 6 Lakh Retail Investors Are Caught in the Wreckage
markets-finance.excerpt: The Pune-based auto software company's surprise profit warning, driven by sudden European OEM spending cuts, triggers JPMorgan downgrade and drags peers Tata Elxsi and LTTS down with it — a cautionary tale for NRI investors in India's mid-cap IT story
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock trading screen showing market data — KPIT Technologies shares crashed 17% to a near four-year low on July 1, 2026
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRI investors with exposure to Indian mid-cap IT mutual funds are directly affected — KPIT's crash reveals the concentration risk in thematic auto-tech bets and raises questions about whether the broader Indian IT services sector faces structural headwinds from European demand weakness and AI disruption
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Salah Chipped a Panenka. Two Australians Missed. Egypt Made History in Dallas.
sports.excerpt: Mohamed Salah fought through a hamstring strain, scored the nerviest penalty of the shootout, and led Egypt to their first-ever World Cup knockout win — a 4-2 shootout victory over Australia in front of 70,244 fans at AT&T Stadium.
sports.image_caption: Mohamed Salah in action for Egypt's national football team
sports.nri_angle: The match was played at AT&T Stadium in the DFW metroplex — home to one of America's largest NRI communities — while NRIs in Australia saw the Socceroos eliminated from the World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Kohli Is Back. Rohit Is Back. Bumrah Is Back. Gill Will Lead India Into England — and Toward the 2027 World Cup.

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Face Elevated Heart Risk by Age 45 Despite Healthier Habits — and the Paradox Runs Deeper Than Diet
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark US study of 2,700 adults finds that South Asian Americans have nearly eight times the prediabetes rate of white peers by midlife — even with better diets and less alcohol. The risk may start at birth.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Cardiovascular screening — new research shows South Asians face elevated heart disease risk by age 45 despite healthier habits (Wikimedia Commons)

sources.label: Journal of the American Heart Association (Feb. 2026)
South Asian Birth Cohort Study, McMaster University

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Directly impacts the 5.4 million Indian Americans and broader South Asian diaspora — the study reveals they need earlier cardiovascular screening starting in their 40s, not the standard mid-50s guidelines.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Having Weak Muscles and Excess Body Fat Dramatically Raises Your Dementia Risk — and South Asians May Be Uniquely Vulnerable
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A landmark Curtin University study of nearly 500,000 adults finds sarcopenic obesity is a major dementia driver, while being overweight alone is not — if muscle strength is preserved
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult performing resistance training, which new research suggests is critical for protecting brain health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians' well-documented 'skinny fat' phenotype — high visceral fat with low muscle mass — places them at elevated risk for the sarcopenic obesity now linked to dementia, making resistance training an urgent priority for NRI health.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Teen's Friends May Shape Their Mental Health More Than You Think — A 600,000-Person Study Shows How

lifestyle-health.image_caption: Teenagers at school — a 600,000-person Finnish study found peer relationships significantly affect adolescent mental health risk (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRI parents raising teenagers in Western school systems face a peer-influence dynamic that differs sharply from Indian schooling — understanding how their child's social environment shapes mental health risk is essential for early intervention.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Fish Oil Supplements Don't Protect Your Brain From Alzheimer's, a Rigorous Two-Year Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Americans spend over $1 billion a year on fish oil, but a USC clinical trial shows the supplements fail to slow cognitive decline — even though they reach the brain. For South Asians, the findings raise uncomfortable questions about a supplement many families swear by.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fish oil capsules, among the most popular dietary supplements worldwide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face rising Alzheimer's risk and are heavy fish oil users — this trial suggests they should shift spending from supplements to whole-food diets.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Remote Work Is Making Americans Lonelier and More Depressed — and the Effect Is Worst for Those Who Live Alone

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech workers in the US are disproportionately in remotable jobs and far from family — making them especially vulnerable to the isolation the study documents.

lifestyle-health.title: Older Adults Who Walk Like Someone 30 Years Younger Have Half the Risk of Cognitive Decline — Even With Alzheimer's Pathology

lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated diabetes and cardiovascular risk that accelerate cognitive decline; walking speed is a culturally familiar, measurable biomarker diaspora families can track as parents age.

food.excerpt: From Malai's masala chai scoops in Manhattan to Kesar Creamery's gulab jamun gelato in Texas, Indian-inspired ice cream brands are reshaping the American frozen dessert landscape — and making NRIs feel right at home.

food.nri_angle: Indian-American entrepreneurs are bringing the tastes of home — kulfi, falooda, saffron pistachio — to mainstream American ice cream shops, giving NRIs nostalgic flavours and normalising Indian desserts for a wider audience.

food.title: Baked Oats Chaat to Rasmalai Tres Leches: India's Viral Fusion Recipes Are Rewriting the Global Cookbook
food.excerpt: A new generation of Indian food creators is mashing up dosa with gochujang, rasmalai with tres leches, and ragi with chocolate lava cake — and racking up tens of millions of views in the process.

food.nri_angle: NRI home cooks are recreating India's viral fusion recipes with ingredients from Patel Brothers and Amazon, adapting them to American kitchens and contributing to a global feedback loop that is making Indian food culture more dynamic than ever.

food.title: From a Family Clay Oven to a James Beard Nod: The Immigrant Story Behind Las Vegas's Hottest Indian Restaurant
food.excerpt: Tamba — named for the Hindi word for copper — earned a Best New Restaurant finalist nod from the James Beard Foundation in its first year, capping a three-decade journey that began with an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant.
food.image_caption: A traditional tandoor clay oven, the centrepiece of Indian cooking that gave the Dhillon family's first restaurant its name
food.nri_angle: Tamba's journey from an immigrant couple's modest Monterey restaurant to a James Beard Best New Restaurant finalist mirrors the larger arc of Indian cuisine's ascent in America, offering diaspora families a powerful narrative of generational ambition rewarded.

food.title: Britannia, Bikano, and Beyond: Indian Snack Brands Storm the American Grocery Aisle
food.excerpt: From Walmart's $10 billion India sourcing pledge to Truly Indian's 1,300-store blitz, packaged Indian food is carving out shelf space that restaurants alone never could.
food.image_caption: Indian packaged snacks — brands like Britannia, Bikano, and Haldiram's are expanding aggressively into American grocery aisles
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who once drove 45 minutes to the nearest desi grocery store for a packet of Good Day biscuits, seeing Britannia and Bikano on Walmart shelves is nothing short of a cultural arrival.

food.title: Haldi Doodh to Herb of the Year: How India's Golden Spice Conquered American Wellness
food.excerpt: The International Herb Association has crowned turmeric the 2026 Herb of the Year, completing a journey from Indian grandmothers' kitchens to Whole Foods shelves and $7 lattes.
food.image_caption: Vibrant golden turmeric powder, the spice crowned 2026 Herb of the Year
food.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up being force-fed haldi doodh, watching turmeric become a $7 cafe latte and official Herb of the Year is a bittersweet vindication of the traditions they once dismissed.

food.title: The Fake Dosa Makers: How AI-Generated Videos Are Weaponising Indian Street Food
food.excerpt: Millions of views, zero reality — AI-generated clips depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are going viral, and the diaspora is paying the reputational price.
food.image_caption: Sev puri chaat, a real Indian street food dish — vibrant, hygienic, and made with craft
food.nri_angle: AI-generated fake videos depicting unsanitary Indian food preparation are fuelling anti-Indian stereotypes online, undercutting the diaspora's decades-long effort to gain respect for Indian cuisine in the West.

food.title: The $24 Bag of Rice: How US Tariffs Are Reshaping the Desi Pantry
food.excerpt: With US duties on Indian goods at 50 percent, staples from Sona Masoori rice to filter coffee have surged in price — and Pakistani brands are quietly filling the gap.
food.image_caption: Basmati rice, a staple of the Indian diaspora pantry now facing steep US tariff hikes (Wikimedia Commons)
food.nri_angle: The 50 percent US tariff on Indian goods is directly hitting NRI family budgets, turning everyday pantry staples like rice, dal, and coffee into luxury items.

food.title: From Pani Puri to Prix Fixe: Sujan Sarkar's Michelin Empire Lands in New York and Phoenix
food.excerpt: The first Bengali chef to earn a Michelin star in America opens two restaurants in five weeks, stretching Indian fine dining from Hudson Yards to the Arizona desert.
food.image_caption: Pani puri served at an Indian restaurant, a dish Sarkar has reimagined as an oyster course
food.nri_angle: Sarkar's expansion from Chicago to New York and Phoenix proves Indian fine dining is now viable beyond coastal food capitals, giving NRIs across America access to world-class Indian cuisine.

food.title: Chicken Stock in Dal Makhani? A Former MasterChef Judge Just Ignited Indian Food's Loudest Fight
food.excerpt: George Calombaris's Instagram reel adding chicken stock cubes to dal makhani has reignited the perennial debate over who gets to reinterpret Indian classics — and where the red line sits.

food.nri_angle: For NRIs who grew up eating their mother's dal makhani, the controversy touches a nerve about cultural ownership and whether Western chefs dilute Indian food's identity as it goes global.

food.excerpt: A new wave of Indian restaurants is quietly spreading into mid-sized American cities far from the coastal corridors, driven by immigrant families betting on untapped appetites.
